“I once joined the wrong class at a dance studio. I thought I was in the right place, so I started following along with everyone. I was watching their feet, trying to work out what I was supposed to be doing, and they all seemed to know what came next. I thought, well, perhaps I’m just slower at picking this up.

“Then I realized it wasn’t the class I’d meant to join. That was the embarrassing part—I’d been trying so hard to keep up instead of checking. Suddenly I didn’t know where to look. You want to leave, but leaving means making it obvious you were in the wrong place. I don’t know whether anyone was paying much attention to me, but it certainly felt as though they might be.”
